text:
David recoiled from the spectral glimpse of rusted gears and empty plinth, the cold, alien logic of the depths seeping into his bones. The murmurs intensified, no longer distinct voices but a single, unsettlingly fluid chorus, as if a thousand tongues had learned to speak as one, echoing the 'foundation completed' and 'architects repaid' with a sinister cadence. They weren't just the voices of the taken, or the echoes of Iris; they were the collective sigh of an ancient, parasitic market finally making good on its investments, each lost soul a dividend. The sheer, impossible scale of the transaction made his breath catch. He was not just watching a story unfold; he was witnessing the true debut of a new, horrifying economic order, one that would make Blackwood Bay's reality a mere casualty.

The dust-caked digital alarm clock, defying all sense, flickered anew, its red digits scrambling before locking into the precise, alien sequence of '7297.49'. It hung in the air, a final, unchallengeable tally. This wasn't merely Elias Thorne leveraging a fallen architect; this was Thorne as a broker, facilitating a transaction with something far older than human commerce, a 'strange friendship' where Blackwood Bay itself was the collateral. The realization hit him like a physical blow: the Undertow wasn’t a force of nature, or even a monster in the conventional sense. It was a market correction, an entity that dealt in stories and memories, rebuilding its empire from the 'foundations' of other, fallen worlds. The hum of the cabin deepened, now carrying an almost musical quality, a morbid lullaby that promised an absolute demolition, a final therapy of the unbuilt.
